name: Verapamil
drug_class: Non-dihydropyridine (phenylalkylamine) calcium channel blocker; class IV antiarrhythmic
route_note: oral immediate- and extended-release; IV for supraventricular tachycardia

discovery.note: Synthesised as a coronary dilator; Albrecht Fleckenstein identified its calcium-antagonist action in the mid-1960s.

tagline: The first calcium channel blocker, a class IV antiarrhythmic
summary: Verapamil was the first calcium channel blocker to be characterised and acts predominantly on the heart. It treats supraventricular arrhythmias, angina and hypertension, and is used off-label to prevent cluster headache.
mechanism: Verapamil blocks L-type calcium channels from the intracellular side in a use-dependent manner, so it acts most strongly on rapidly firing tissue. It slows the SA node and markedly prolongs AV nodal conduction and refractoriness, which terminates re-entrant SVT and slows ventricular rate in AF.
It reduces myocardial contractility and dilates coronary and peripheral arteries. It also inhibits P-glycoprotein and CYP3A4, causing many drug interactions.
uses: Atrial fibrillation or flutter rate control

history.title: Synthesis
history.detail: Verapamil is synthesised at Knoll AG.

history.title: Calcium antagonism
history.detail: Albrecht Fleckenstein's laboratory begins showing that verapamil blocks excitation–contraction coupling by inhibiting calcium entry.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Approved in the US, among the first calcium channel blockers there.

history.title: DAVIT II
history.detail: Verapamil after MI reduces reinfarction in patients without heart failure.

history.title: Type 1 diabetes pilot
history.detail: A small randomised trial reports that verapamil helps preserve beta-cell function in recent-onset type 1 diabetes, prompting larger studies.

serious: Ventricular fibrillation if given IV in wide-complex tachycardia or WPW with AF

facts: IV verapamil can be fatal in ventricular tachycardia misdiagnosed as SVT.
Constipation is its most characteristic side effect.
